laws.rule: In the station plazas of Mito, Akatsuka and Uchihara stations (including the Mito Station north and south exit decks), Mito City bans smoking outside the plaza smoking areas, skateboarding and roller skating, setting up stalls for profit, lighting fires, and climbing trees or statues. Visitors must not sleep there, put up posters, or block slopes, handrails, tactile paving or lifts, and should use loudspeakers with care for others. Handing out leaflets or collecting signatures needs the city's permission. Someone who ignores a warning and then an order can be fined up to JPY 50,000 (about A$451.18, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82).

laws.rule: Tsukuba City bans smoking on the street in five designated areas: around Tsukuba Station, Kenkyu-Gakuen Station, Expo Memorial Park, Midori no Eki, and the approach street to Mt Tsukuba Shrine. The fine is JPY 2,000 (about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026). Littering is banned citywide; in the busy station areas a warning and a stop order come first, then a JPY 2,000 fine. Graffiti on public buildings or structures carries a JPY 50,000 fine (about A$451.18).

Ibaraki Ordinance on the Healthy Development of Young People (茨城県青少年の健全育成等に関する条例), art. 33. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 11 pm to 4 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period without special reason; the guardian's own duty has no penalty. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.

festivals.what: Ofune Matsuri (Kashima Jingu, Kashima City): a great festival held once every 12 years, in the year of the horse, when the shrine's deity travels about 30 km by land and by boat (via Itako Quay), met by Katori Shrine at Katoshu in Katori City. It was held on 1 to 3 September 2026 (main day 2 September), with traffic controls on all three days; the next, counting the 12-year cycle, would fall in 2038. Each 1 September the shrine also holds its annual festival (reitaisai) with an Imperial envoy.
